- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) and price drops, model often undercorrects; add 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.  
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 1–2 standard deviations below recent mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward adjustment of 1–2% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction by 1–3% for 3–5 days.
